title: Mid-cycle contract adjustments: credit reversals, grace periods, and usage reclassification
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a predictable operational workflow for handling mid-cycle enterprise contract changes that affect billing: retroactive credit reversals, temporary grace periods for overages, and reclassification of usage between invoiced buckets. Deliverables: policy doc for CS/Finance, API contract for automated reversals, UI flows for console adjustments, audit/logging changes for Private deployments, and acceptance tests tied to sample enterprise contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc approved by Finance and Legal and published to Confluence
Automated reversal API implements idempotent reversal endpoint and is covered by unit + integration tests
Console UI shows pending reversal state and a one-click approve/reject for Finance users
All reversals generate audit events with original invoice linkage (invoice_id) and reason code
Sample contracts run through end-to-end playbook (create change -> generate reversal -> reconcile to ledger) with zero data loss
tasks: Draft policy and playbook for credit reversal scenarios (owner: Aisha)
Spec API endpoint for /billing/reversals with payload schema and auth model (owner: Liam)
Design console flows for pending reversals and temporary grace toggles (owner: Maya - Design)
Implement backend handler and ledger adjustments (owner: ENG-3022 team)
Build e2e test harness using sandbox enterprise account (owner: QA)
Coordinate with Sales/Legal to map contract clauses to automation triggers (owner: Product)
decisions: Use forgiveness window (grace period) as default 7 days unless overridden by contract clause
Automated reversals will be idempotent and surfaced as 'pending_reversal' until Finance approves for >$5k credits
We will not retroactively change past tax calculations; instead create offset credit lines and link to original invoice
Reclassification of usage buckets will only occur for usage misclassification (metering error) and require a ledger reconciliation run

notes: Edge cases to cover: mid-cycle plan downgrade where committed reserved capacity should be partially refunded versus converted to credits; inter-region invoices where tax jurisdictions differ; refunds for prepaid enterprise credits.
Operational runbook should include SLA targets for Finance response (72 hours) and a tagging scheme for escalations.
Consider building a 'reversal dry run' mode that simulates ledger adjustments without committing to production to give Finance visibility into downstream tax and revenue recognition impact.
